description.narrative:
General Objective (Impact - long-term) Contribute to the sustainable closure of the urban water cycle in a sustainable way, with a focus on resource recovery, protecting and preserving ecosystems that improve people's quality of life.
Specific Objective Promote the upscaling and replication of sustainable sanitation service models in Bolivian municipalities, leveraging local resources and with other funders, articulating actions with the central government through the Vice Ministry of Water and Sanitation.
The implementation of the second phase of the program will be executed through three Outcomes: - Outcome 1: Support for public policies in the sector at the national level - Outcome 2: Optimization and sustainability of sanitation services - Outcome 3: Evaluation and validation of the implemented models

Programmet syftar till att skapa hållbara kretslopp av städernas vattenhantering, med fokus på resursåtervinning, skydd och bevarande av ekosystem som förbättrar människors livskvalitet. Specifikt mål: Främja expansion och replikering av hållbara sanitetstjänstmodeller i bolivianska kommuner, som växlar upp med lokal finansiella medel samt med andra externa finansiärer, genom samverkan och koordinering av insatser med centralregeringen genom vice ministeriet för vatten och sanitet. Genomförandet av den andra fasen av programmet kommer att genomföras genom tre resultat: 1) Stöd till offentlig politik inom VA-sektorn på nationell nivå; 2) Optimering och ökad hållbarhet av sanitetstjänster; 3) Utvärdering och validering av implementerade modeller. Programmet kommer genom sitt fokus dessutom bidra till mer hållbar vattenresurshantering, klimatanpassning, minskade klimatutsläpp, och minskade utsläpp av orenat avloppsvatten.

The program aims to contribute to sustainable closure of urban water cycles, with a focus on resource recovery, protection and preservation of ecosystems that improve people's quality of life. Specific objective: Promote the expansion and replication of sustainable sanitation service models in Bolivian municipalities, leveraging with local financial resources as well as with other external financiers, through collaboration and coordination of efforts with the central government through the Deputy Ministry of Water and Sanitation. The implementation of this second phase of the program will be implemented through three outcomes: 1) Support for public policies in the water and wastewater sector at national level; 2) Optimization and increased sustainability of sanitation services; 3) Evaluation and validation of implemented models. Through its focus, the program will also contribute to more sustainable water resource management, climate adaptation, reduced climate emissions, and reduced emissions of untreated wastewater.

Examples of what has been achieved during the first phase of the program are as follows:
- Strategic sanitation planning implemented in two cities, Cliza and Tarija.
- A management model of WWTPs (wastewater treatment plants) in the municipality of Cliza that treat 100% of the generated wastewater.
- Two faecal sludge management models implemented, one in the municipality of Montero and another in Cliza.
- Developing an industrial WWTP for the municipal slaughterhouse of Tarija; the first of its kind in the country.
- Supporting the development of a sustainable collection and treatment service for dry toilet systems in El Alto and decentralized WWTPs in the community of Chinchaya, La Paz.
- Active collaboration and exchange with global water and sanitation networks such as SuSanA (Sustainable Sanitation Alliance), FSMA (Faecal Sludge Management Alliance), and Sanitation and Water for All.
The second phase of the program that initiated in July 2023, had until June 2024 the following main advances:
Development of public policies, with ongoing collaboration on:
- Support to the implementation of the National Strategy for Treatment Plants (ENTAR) with Ministry of Environment and Water.
- Support to the National Authority for Water and Sanitation (AAPS) in the validation and improvement of the performance indicators of the regulated WWTPs for their inspection.
- Development of national design guidelines for decentralized WWTPs and sludge management.
Technical assistance processes, such as:
- Exchange of experiences, with more than 400 persons visiting the WWTPs in Cliza since July 2023, representing municipalities, national authorities, donors, NGOs, universities, among others.
- Strategic sanitation planning under way for Oruro Technical designs of decentralized WWTP's e.g. in La Paz, Oruro and Tarija
Knowledge management, research, and innovation:
- Aguatuya continues leading the SuSanA's Latin American Regional Chapter.
- New agreements for collaboration with universities.
- Validation studies: ww reuse products application in crop production, production plan and market for reuse products (in preparation), and training of farmers and municipal technicians in the application of ww reuse products.
The second phase of the program had until June 2025 the following main advances:
Outcome 1: Support for public policy in the sector at the national level
Working with the AAPS
- Support for wastewater sampling in 11 regulated EPSAS in the departments of La Paz, Cochabamba, Santa Cruz and Oruro
Exchange of experiences
- Experience exchange is a very important practice that allows direct learning with treatment plant solutions that are in operation, it can show how common problems were solved and inspires visitors to come up with new ideas in their workplaces. From January to June 2025, the WWTPs in the Valle Alto received 95 people from different municipalities in Bolivia, as well as the visit of Sanima, an NGO that works in the periurban areas of Lima.
Outcome 2: Optimization and sustainability of sanitation services
Strategic sanitation planning
- In May, the consultant Tomaz Quipnis visited to train technicians from Aguatuya and continue with the development of the strategic sanitation plan for Oruro. A meeting was held with the Mayor of Oruro to present the progress of the work, another meeting with technicians from the Municipality and a third with technicians from the Oruro water services company SELA.
Technical Assistance to Small Municipalities
- The WWTP projects for the urban center of Sacabamba and for the community of Matarani were concluded and delivered, the elaboration of the Toro Toro project was canceled.
Technical assistance to the municipalities of intermediate cities
- For the municipality of Tarija, a second WWTP project has been developed in the Torrecillas sector, the project was delivered to the municipality in June, and has the support of the entire population of the sector for its implementation, the specific agreement to start the construction of the WWTP is in approval.
- With the delivery of the faecal sludge project for Tolomosita, and the approval of a specific agreement with the Municipality of Tarija, the PTLF is under construction, the financing for this stage is from MEDICOR.
- With the protocol delivery of the project in Chicani and Chinchaya, they are scheduled to be launched from August 2025.
- April, the industrial water treatment plant of the Tarija Slaughterhouse was delivered, and it is currently in the startup phase.
SuSaNa Latin America Network
- Meetings with Focal Points for Water Week Planning
- Publications of the biannual newsletter of SuSanA Latin America
- Discussion and screening of the film "Holy Shit: The Regenerative Revolution", held in February 2025.
Work with academia, lbnorca
- In coordination with the UPB, two scientific articles are being prepared on "Potential of a UASBplus-Activated Sludge Hydro System for the Treatment of Domestic Wastewater", in the case of Ucureña and "Performance Evaluation of a Plant municipal wastewater treatment configured by USB's and trickling filters".
- lbnorca; During the first half of 2025, 2 national technical standards on wastewater treatment processes have been published. There are 4 documents in work for its subsequent approval and publication, both in wastewater treatment and in fecal sludge management.
Outcome 3: Evaluation, innovation and validation of the implemented models
Proinpa
- Based on the 2024 report, research continued on the biofertilizer/biofungicide produced in the Cliza sludge plant, to verify the efficiency of the biofertilizer in the elimination of the Chaqui fungus, a disease that attacks the maiz plant, so demonstration plots of maiz and potato were implemented to reach a greater number of communities and producers in Cliza with the product.
- In a tripartite way (Aguatuya, PROINPA and the GAM Cliza), a mechanism is being developed that allows the production and marketing, in a sustainable way, of this product throughout the municipality of Cliza.
Renewable energy
- The energy efficiency study is being carried out in the Ucureña WWTP with the UPB, in this semester fieldwork was carried out for the collection of data on the operation of solar panels (voltage, amperage), operation of pumps and motors and mediation of the variation of flows at different times.
During the last fase, up to 31 July 2026 , the following results can be highlighted:
Outcome 1: Support for public policy in the sector at the national level
Work at a national level
The Bolivia con Agua Platform continues to make progress, though not at the pace they had hoped for; a larger number of institutions working in the sector have joined the platform.
Support for the Vice Ministry of Water and Sanitation through emergency projects in Santa Cruz (Samaipata), including technical assistance and the provision of two water tanks.
They supported the AAPS in collecting wastewater samples from 14 regulated EPSAS in the departments of Cochabamba, Santa Cruz, Oruro, Beni, Tarija, and Potosí; they also provided support for the 2025 report on the performance indicators of wastewater treatment plants (PTARs).
Exchange of experiences Learning about successful, operational projects is very important for people who visit the Aguatuya wastewater treatment plants; they can see firsthand that there are no unpleasant odours and verify the quality of the treated water. During these exchange visits, Aguatuya have hosted delegations from various institutions from the departments of Santa Cruz, Tarija, La Paz, Oruro, and Potosí. These institutions include municipal governments, universities, NGOs, private companies, OTBs, and EPSAs.
Outcome 2: Optimisation and sustainability of sanitation services
Strategic sanitation planning
The Strategic Sanitation Plan for the Municipality of Oruro has been completed; it has now been designed and printed. This brings the total number of plans completed under this Phase II to two: Tarija and Oruro. In the case of the Municipality of Tarija, this plan forms the basis on which the implementation of decentralised treatment plants is being carried out, as well as the Tolomosita sludge treatment plant.
Technical Assistance to Small Municipalities Arbieto and Toco Arbieto still to be completed. Works in Toco were cancelled owing to a lack of consensus regarding the site.
Technical Assistance to Intermediate-City Municipalities The Torrecillas Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) in the Municipality of Tarija has been completed. Implementation of the municipal counterpart contribution is still outstanding, after which the plant will be commissioned; under the specific agreement signed, this must be completed by December 2026. During this half-year, the commissioning of the Chicani and Chinchaya plants was completed. Operators were trained, and both plants are now fully operational. The SEI Watershed Project has implemented a drip-irrigation pilot scheme in the area.
In June 2026, commissioning of the Industrial Wastewater Treatment Plant (IND-WWTP) at the Tarija Municipal Slaughterhouse was completed. The following activities were carried out:
- Training of operational staff and definition of roles - Calibration, inspection and automation of equipment - Validation and optimisation of the SCADA system - Formation, growth and stabilisation of biomass in the biological reactor (SBR) - Foam and sludge management - Operation and optimisation of the biological reactor (SBR) - Monitoring campaigns
The Autonomous Municipal Government (GAM) of Tarija has requested that Aguatuya monitor and evaluate the performance of the IND-WWTP until the end of 2026; these commitments have been set out in a specific agreement.
SuSanA Latin America Network The actions driven by SuSanA and regionally coordinated by Aguatuya have achieved the following:
-Positioned Bolivia as a regional benchmark in sustainable sanitation -Strengthened SouthSouth exchange
-Integrated Latin Americas voice, through a representative from Brazil, on the SuSanA Global Steering Committee -Consolidated an active Latin American network -Generated influence in global decision-making spaces -Promoted innovative models of circular economy and nutrient recovery -Opened up opportunities for international funding and technical cooperation.
The impact of SuSanA goes beyond technical exchange: it has helped build a global community of learning and collaboration that connects local experiences with international sustainability and climate resilience agendas.
Work with the Academia and Ibnorca Scientific backing is of the utmost importance in consolidating these models. To this end, Agustuya have worked with the Universidad Privada Boliviana (UPB), which has carried out the following studies during 2026:
- An evaluation study of the photovoltaic (solar panel) system at the Ucureña Wastewater Treatment Plant - A study of alkalising agents sodium hydroxide and calcium hydroxide for the pH conditioning of effluents generated at the Tarija Municipal Abattoir. The main objective is to adjust the pH to a range of 7.59, a value that ensures suitable conditions for subsequent biological processes - A characterisation study of refractory organic matter in the wastewater from the Ucureña and Tolata wastewater treatment plants - Aguatuya also have signed agreements in place with the Universidad Mayor de San Andrés (UMSA), where two theses are currently being developed; with the Universidad Católica Boliviana (UCB), which carried out the study of the Urine Treatment Plant in El Alto; and with UGRM (Universidad Autónoma Gabriel René Moreno), where two theses are being developed on the Montero Sludge Treatment Plant.
Outcome 3: Evaluation, Innovation and Validation Montero Sludge Plant Among the most important conclusions, the Montero Faecal Sludge Treatment Plant (PTLF) constitutes a relevant pilot experience for decentralised sanitation in Bolivia. Its value is not limited to the infrastructure built: it also generates local evidence, links COSMOL with academia, and opens up a concrete pathway for the safe recovery of organic matter and nutrients. The monitoring carried out confirms significant progress in the quality of the liquid effluent and shows that the treated sludge has very promising characteristics as a soil conditioner. The next stage should focus on institutionalising monitoring, validating controlled agricultural uses, and ensuring the operational and financial sustainability of the service.
Urine Treatment Plant, El Alto The evaluation was carried out with the Universidad Católica Boliviana (UCB), which demonstrated that the precipitation process at the urine treatment plant has a high capacity for phosphorus recovery, achieving an approximate 97% reduction in phosphorus concentration in the supernatant (from 640.1 to 16.5 mg P/L). The high phosphorus concentration in the sediment (7,361.3 mg P/L) confirms the efficiency of the magnesium oxide precipitation process in forming phosphate minerals, mainly struvite.
The process yielded a solid fertiliser enriched in phosphorus and magnesium, while nitrogen recovery was only partial. The nitrogen content of the filter cake ranged between 0.52% and 0.76%, values consistent with fertilisers obtained through struvite precipitation, which provide nitrogen as a complementary nutrient alongside phosphorus and magnesium.
Cliza Sludge Plant "Villacar" By-product The initiative planned with PROINPA demonstrated that the sludge treated at the Villa El Carmen plant can cease to be an environmental liability and become a valuable agricultural input. The Villacar biofertiliser/biofungicide showed a biocontrol effect against fungal diseases, along with a nutritional contribution that translated into measurable yield improvements, while the compost derived from dried sludge showed benefits for potato crops, vegetables, and urban green areas.
The proposed management model is a public-private partnership between PROINPA, the Autonomous Municipal Government (GAM) of Cliza, and Aguatuya, which is currently being established.
